reviews.snippet: It made me sad, because the manager was so nice, but the ribs are bone-in jerky. I have never had to fight or gnaw to get pork off of a rib like that before. I made my self eat it because I paid $30 for 4 ribs. It made me miss KY (fall off the bone with tacky sauce covering the top). These were dehydrated and caked in cracked pepper. The boiled corn, free bread, and pickles were nice though.

reviews.snippet: They served me more than I expected after telling them this was my first time having bbq in Texas. Definitely a tourist trap. Brisket, and ribs were dry and over salted. Sides were average. I’m sure there are much better BBQ joints in town.

reviews.snippet: Staff are extremely aggressive in trying to sell more (very expensive) food by the pound than you can possibly eat or want.  Menu options aren't clear and staff are extremely impatient as customers try to understand the options and pricing.  I told them I wanted 1/4 pound so they cut off 1/2 pound and told me I needed to take that.  They angrily cut it down to 1/4 pound only when I firmly refused.  One lady in our group was sold 2lbs of brisket for a total of $80 when she couldn't possibly eat, or afford, more than 1/4 lb.

reviews.snippet:
I've traveled to a lot of places and consider myself not to have a picky palate. Cooper's was recommended to us by a local resident...AFTER I insisted that I preferred Rudy's BBQ, as I tried it in New Mexico and enjoyed it.

They insisted that Cooper's was a must try. Since I wanted to give something new a try...boy were we WRONG.

Cooper's BBQ isn't the spot. The food is HORRIBLE and very costly. Very bland, "raisins in the potatoe salad" nasty. If you feel my drift.

I had one beef rib, pork loin, bacon and Jalapeño mac and cheese,  and some banana pudding.  The bill came to over $51.00

Tried to put BBQ sauce on it, and it literally was watery based hot sauce. Very runny. I'm confused on the 5 star reviews.

I agree with the review from Dimtry located below... Beef Rib was flavorless, dry, and very hard to chew/cut. Tried to put BBQ sauce on it to maybe help the taste...nah. Didn't help.

Sorry Austin. If this place is your "Best version" of Texas BBQ...then you'd might-as-well eat a McRib from McDonald's.  (Never had one).

It had mobile pay-to-park for $2.90 Clean restaurant,  Texas BBQ themed restaurant with a friendly staff...but this

This review is only based on the food.

reviews.snippet: Visited as an out-of-towner and had one of the most unwelcoming experiences I’ve ever had at a bar. I simply asked how much our beers were — a completely normal question — and was met with an aggressive, condescending response from what appeared to be a bartender or manager. He said “do you have a problem? Maybe you should leave,” and when I explained I was just asking a question, he told me I “shouldn’t ask so many questions.” The dismissive, misogynistic attitude was shocking and completely unprofessional. We left and will not be returning. If you’re visiting from out of town, I’d look elsewhere.
